old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-era9","title":"C capability table: floor ledger not bounded (diverges from Python/Rust)","description":"Discovered reviewing p7mv. lichen/subsys/lichen/gateway/capability_announce.c floor_raise() appends to a fixed CONFIG_LICHEN_CAPABILITY_TABLE_CAPACITY floor ledger and silently drops new floors when full ('ledger full; live entries still pin their own seq'). Python CapabilityTable._bound_floors and Rust bound_seq_floors actively prune the ledger (drop the lowest-IID floor whose IID is no longer a live entry) so it stays bounded by live eviction churn. The C version never prunes, so long-gone IIDs permanently consume floor slots and eventually block anti-replay floors for genuinely-evicted IIDs (rollback-protection gap under sustained churn). Note: Python/Rust RETAIN floors for live entries (cached_seq returns max(entry.seq, floor)); the prune only targets floors for IIDs no longer resident. Implement floor_prune matching that semantic + a host test cycling \u003ecapacity evictions.
